How to Use This Book
This book is written for you, not for the child. Each unit gives you the science in plain words, the exact sentences you can say out loud, the
mistakes children usually make, and one activity you can do with things already in your kitchen.
Five rules that make it work
1. Ten to fifteen minutes at a time. A six-year-old's attention is short. Two short sessions in a week beat one long one.
2. Touch first, write second. Let him hold it, shake it, drop it in water, squash it — then open the book and answer the questions.
3. Ask "What do you think will happen?" before every experiment. Write his guess down. A wrong guess is not a failure; it is the beginning of
science.
4. Let him find the answer himself. When you tell him the answer, he remembers it for a day. When he discovers it, he remembers it for years.
5. Praise the trying, not the knowing. "You looked really carefully" works better than "You're so clever."
How each unit is laid out
Section What it is for
The Big Idea The one thing your child must walk away knowing.
Say It Like This Words you can read aloud, already at a six-year-old's level.
Watch Out For The mistake almost every child makes here, and how to correct it gently.
Try It at Home A hands-on activity using household items.
Key Words The words to repeat until they stick.
Questions Six questions to do together after the activity.
A note about the questions
Read each question aloud and let your child answer in his own words first. Then help him write. At this age, speaking the answer counts
just as much as writing it. All the answers are gathered at the back of this book, starting on the Answer Key page.
Safety, every time
An adult stays with the child for every activity. No glass, no sockets, no flames, and nothing small enough to swallow is left with a child
alone. Water activities are done in a bowl or the sink, never near electrical items.
